finding.claim: A callback URL stored from an untrusted subscribe request is later used as the destination of a server-side POST with no validation, letting an attacker make the server send requests to internal hosts (localhost, 169.254.169.254, private services). Blind SSRF: the response is discarded and never returned to the attacker.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(), documented at Jobs.java:12 as the body of POST /subscribe (attacker-controlled; the HTTP handler is not in this directory, so this is inferred from the comment)
finding.sink: URI.create(cb) at Jobs.java:21 used as the target of client.send(...) at Jobs.java:24

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe body includes callbackUrl
subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl) accepts the value unchanged
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it with no checks
notifyAll(String payload) runs every minute (comment at line 17)
URI.create(cb) parses the stored value as the request target
POST body is the server-supplied payload; attacker cannot set the body
client.send(...) issues the request; response discarded

finding.guards_checked: subscribe(): none (no scheme, host, port, IP range, or allowlist check). notifyAll(): none (no re-validation before send). Scheme: HttpClient only supports http/https, so file:// and other schemes fail, but host is unrestricted. Redirects: HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so redirects are not followed; this does not block a direct request to an internal host. DNS rebinding and private-IP blocking: none present. Excluded: thumb() at Jobs.java:29-35 is not a finding: the regex full-match fixes scheme and host to cdn.example.com and allows only [a-z0-9] in the path, leaving no @, /, .., or ? to exploit, and redirects are not followed.

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe() (Jobs.java:13-14) stores callbackUrl unchanged, and notifyAll() (Jobs.java:18-25) calls URI.create(cb) and client.send with no host, scheme, IP, or allowlist check. The only validation in the file is in thumb() (Jobs.java:30), which is not on this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (comment at Jobs.java:12, storage at 14, sink at 21-24, no guard on the path), but the attacker-control claim rests only on the comment at Jobs.java:12 ("POST /subscribe body: name, callbackUrl"), and the HTTP handler that exposes subscribe() is not in the directory, so I cannot confirm that an unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can reach it.
